subject: Regional peering + egress proxy implementation plan and next steps
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@dataforge.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>; Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@datacove.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: low-latency multi-region connectivity and auth questions

Thanks for the call today — quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the PoC: 

Summary of our needs:
- Low tail latency for chat/assist (99th percentile ~120ms target from US west coast)
- Multi-region presence (us-west + eu-west) with smart routing to nearest region
- Private connectivity: prefer VPC peering or private endpoints; IP allowlist also acceptable as fallback
- Tight egress controls: restrict egress via our proxy, DNS resolution through internal resolvers, and mTLS between our proxy and Redwood if possible
- SDK requirements: we plan to use Redwood SDK with tool-calling and structured JSON outputs; embeddings + a small reranker flow (~5k embeddings/day to start, ramping to 50k)
- Auth: prefer mTLS or OIDC-based short-lived tokens; we need details on cert provisioning and rotation

Clarifying questions:
1) Can Redwood support interface VPC endpoints (AWS) per-region, and if so do you provide stable IP ranges we can allowlist?
2) If we use a regional egress proxy (our side), do you support mutual TLS with customer certs?
3) Any known constraints for structured output / tool-calling when requests go through a proxy?
4) Do you have recommended TTLs for DNS and any special records to ensure proper routing when we failover regions?

Next steps: would like a proposed technical approach and a list of items we need to collect from our infra team (CIDR blocks, proxy certs, expected RPS / concurrency).

--
Alex Turner
Head of Infrastructure, DataForge AI
alex.turner@dataforge.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@dataforge.ai>; Priya Singh <priya.singh@datacove.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: low-latency multi-region connectivity and auth questions

Thanks Alex — great to meet the DataForge team. Quick response and a proposed path for the PoC below. I attached a short playbook and a POA matrix for collection of artifacts.

High-level recommended approach (PoC):
- Regional private endpoints: provision interface endpoints in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 and advertise them to your infra. We typically recommend interface VPCE + customer-side proxy in front of the endpoint for additional egress controls.
- Stable allowlist: Redwood will provide per-region ephemeral IP ranges for the initial PoC window; for production we recommend VPC peer or PrivateLink where stable addressing is enforced.
- mTLS/auth options: two viable patterns:
  1) Mutual TLS with client cert (we can accept certs signed by your CA or issue a short-lived cert via our provisioning flow)
  2) Short-lived OIDC tokens (we can integrate with your identity provider for token exchange)
- SDK + structured output: SDK remains the same. When you route through proxy, ensure it forwards the request body untouched and supports streaming. Structured output and tool-calling work over the same HTTPS path — we just need to make sure request/response size limits are accounted for.
- Embeddings & rerankers: Embedding traffic can flow over the same endpoint; for cost and latency we suggest colocating a caching layer for common embedding vectors and using our reranker endpoint set (we'll provide model-specific hostnames).

Action items we need from DataForge for scoping:
- CIDR ranges for proxies and peered VPCs (include both public egress IPs and private ranges)
- Expected RPS and concurrency per region (tail percentiles if available)
- TLS provisioning preference (mTLS or OIDC) and contact for certs/IDP config
- List of domain names that must resolve internally (for split-horizon DNS)
\Attachments:
- redwood-peering-playbook-v1.pdf (high level design + required artifacts)
- poa-matrix.xlsx (POA with owners and deadlines)
\Proposed timeline:
- Week 1: Exchange CIDRs, certs / IDP config, basic test endpoints
- Week 2: Test connectivity + smoke test with a small traffic sample (chat + embeddings)
- Week 3: Latency tuning (proxy timeouts, DNS TTLs) + run reranker baseline
\I'll sync Ben and Aditya to draft the more detailed technical checklist. If this looks good we'll schedule a 30min handoff with your infra team.

Cheers,

Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>; Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>; Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:46:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Technical plan draft for DataForge PoC

(Internal thread - do not forward to customer without review)

Notes and proposed technical specifics to include in the PoC checklist: 

1) Endpoint types and addressing:
- Use AWS Interface endpoints (Recommended) per region; these will sit in our serving VPCs. We will publish the ENIs' private IPs for customer routing. For initial PoC we can also provide a stable set of NAT egress IPs for allowlisting — see playbook.

2) mTLS flow options:
- Option A: Customer presents client cert; Redwood validates against our CA bundle. Cert rotation can be automated via ACME-like flow we can set up for the PoC.
- Option B: Customer uses a short-lived JWT issued by their IDP; Redwood will validate via OIDC introspection.

3) Proxy behavior and header preservation:
- Customer proxy must preserve x-forwarded-for and a few Redwood headers (we'll document exact header names). Streaming requires HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer or HTTP/2 with proper connection reuse.

4) Structured output/tool-calling implications:
- Tool-calls that contain outbound webhooks require explicit egress allowlisting for the receiving webhooks. If webhooks are internal-only, ensure the proxy can reach them and certs are trusted.

5) Embeddings + reranker:
- Recommend a dedicated embedding host per region; if embeddings are latency sensitive, consider private caching on the customer side for repeated vectors. Reranking can be colocated but watch for cross-region consistency for stateful rerankers.

6) Testing checklist:
- Connectivity: TCP, TLS handshake, cert validation
- Latency: synthetic 99th percentile (50 concurrent connections)
- Functional: structured output parsing and reranker accuracy smoke test

I'll merge these into the playbook and send to Irene for customer-facing copy. Ben, can you share an initial ask for expected QPS so we can size pool?

- Aditya

Thanks Irene — the plan looks good. A couple items from our side: 
- We'll provide CIDR blocks and public egress IPs by EOD Monday (22nd).
- For TLS we'd prefer mTLS for the PoC to validate the full cert path; long-term we may look at short-lived tokens.
- RPS: initial traffic will be ~120 QPS (mixture of chat & embeddings), with spiky loads up to 300 QPS for short bursts. 99th p95 latency target is 120ms from our agents in us-west.

Two quick follow-ups: 
1) Can you confirm whether structured output payloads are size-limited differently when routed through an interface VPCE + proxy?
2) For reranker hostnames you mentioned — can you share the naming convention (so our DNS team can add split-horizon records)?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we'll target the handoff meeting next Tue/Wed.

Alex

Notes: Structured output size — no special service-side limits change when routed through interface VPCE + proxy; the main constraints are HTTP timeouts and proxy body size limits. For PoC we'll request your proxy allow up to 2MB payloads and keep idle timeouts > 90s for streaming sessions.
